newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates mixed in dull trading.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates mixed in dull trading.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates were mixed on Monday in dull trade as spinners kept to the sidelines amid reports that ginners were holding back stocks of more than a million bales, dealers said.

The state Cotton Export Corporation of Pakistan said on Sunday cotton output from the 1996/97 (July-June) crop had reached a provisional 3.464 million 375-lb bales by November 7, up from 2.499 million bales in the same period last year.
It said a total of 1.079 million unsold bales were stocked at ginning factories, up from 722,100 in the year-ago period.
In the kerb market, NIAB-78 variety was traded at 2,200 rupees ($54.69) per maund (37.32 kg), dealers said.
